Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with the workspace contract, then I’ll use the required wake-visual inspection skill to examine current multi-wake keyframes before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring/history sources.

The contract confirms there is one editable solver candidate and one sampled rollout, a `left_domain` failure. The visual-first skill now requires anchoring the keyframes to the observation, metrics, and diagnostics; I’m reading those plus the assigned guidance and inherited optimizer logs before forming a hypothesis.

The numeric evidence says the seed briefly improves range (minimum distance `8.61L`) but then plunges `13.30L` in body/head y and exits after only `50.1` released time units, with very high moment and command effort. I’m now checking whether the keyframes show self-propelled target approach or an uncontrolled wake-driven turn; that distinction will determine the feedback change.

The keyframes resolve the failure mechanism: after release the fish advances leftward at first, then rapidly yaws nose-down into a nearly vertical descent; repeated large-amplitude body bends continue while its head trajectory crosses the lower boundary. It never reaches the cylinder-wake/target region. I’ll now cross-check the per-frame diagnostics and available policy state fields, then write this diagnosis and the candidate hypothesis before editing the controller, as the skill requires.

The sampled candidate is exactly the assigned naive seed, and there are no inherited optimizer notes beyond the unchanged parent guidance and its baseline Elo. Its useful mechanism is measurable upstream self-propulsion; its failure is also concrete: target blindness plus actuator-limit contact lets wake-driven yaw become a lower-boundary dive. I’m recording a bounded bearing-feedback hypothesis with an explicit wrong-sign falsification boundary before changing the policy.

The candidate now keeps the autonomous propulsion oscillator but adds only one new capability: smooth body-frame bearing steering. Its nominal `22°`, `0.75`-period gait is sized to stay below the observed hard rate/acceleration caps. I’m distilling the prior rollout—not this unevaluated candidate—into durable guidance with a clear far-field applicability boundary.

Both required evidence files are now materially updated, and the candidate remains non-empty. I’m invoking the prescribed three-part check runner now: guidance provenance, lightweight Julia policy execution/schema, and edit-boundary validation. No CFD will be run.

The first prescribed check found a workspace-contract rendering defect: `README.md` lists the same copied parent twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. I’m inspecting the checker’s local parsing rule and will make only the minimal metadata repair needed to resolve that ambiguity, then rerun it.

The Julia check did not reach the candidate: this shell’s login profile is broken and `julia` is absent from `PATH` (exit 127). The inherited evaluation log identifies the installed Julia 1.12.2 tree, so I’m locating that executable and will rerun the exact non-CFD check with a non-login shell.

All prescribed checks now pass: guidance provenance, Julia policy execution/parameter schema, and solver edit boundary. The only checker repair was removing the duplicated identical parent entry from the rendered workspace README. No CFD or external research was run.

Completed exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): bounded body-frame bearing steering with a lower-amplitude, slower oscillator intended to avoid sampled actuator saturation.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, metric cross-check, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:27): evidence-backed lesson with far-field applicability limits.

All prescribed checks pass: guidance provenance, Julia contract/schema execution, and solver edit boundary. No CFD was run.
